title: Technology Sector Update for 07/06/2018: SIMO,MRVL,FB,SATS

Technology stocks rode sizable advances on Friday, with shares of tech companies in the S&P 500 adding over 1.2% in value today while the Philadelphia semiconductor index also was posting a more than 1.2% rise.
Among technology companies moving on news:
- Silicon Motion Technology ( SIMO ) retreated Friday, falling over 6% shortly before tonight's closing bell that followed the NAND flash controller and solid-state storage company saying it expects Q2 revenue will be near the midpoint of the current guidance range expecting between $134.3 million to $140.8 million for the three months ended June 30. The Street is at $138.3 million, according to the Capital IQ consensus. Silicon Motion will report its Q2 results soon after the closing bell on July 31.
In other sector news:
+ Facebook ( FB ) has extended its Friday gains, recently climbing over 1%, after reports the social networking company is in talks for what could be its biggest original series yet, a docu-series on soccer superstar Cristiano Ronaldo for Facebook Watch. Citing sources, Variety said Facebook is ready to shell out plenty of money for the project, with Ronaldo reportedly earning around $10 million for the 13-episode show. Ronaldo has been the most popular athlete on Facebook with more than 120 million followers on his official page.
+ Echostar ( SATS ) was slightly more than 1% higher in recent Friday trading after the satellite communications company reportedly is seeking constructive talks with the Inmarsat board of directors after the UK-based company rebuffed its latest takeover offer worth GBP3.2 billion, or about $4.2 billion. Echostar's higher July 3 bid was a mixture of cash and stock valuing Inmarsat GBP5.32 per share. The British firm rejected Echostar's original bid back in June, saying that the proposal significantly undervalued the company. Echostar had until 1700 local, or 12 p.m. ET, on Friday to update its bid.
+ Marvell Technology Group ( MRVL ) was back on positive ground Friday afternoon, erasing a decline as large as 1% that followed the specialty integrated circuits manufacturer completing its $6 billion cash-and-stock acquisition of Cavium Inc. Marvell said will provide an update on Cavium's contribution to its fiscal Q2 and Q3 financial results when it reports its Q2 earnings in early September. The company also said Cavium co-founder and CEO Syed Ali and two other Cavium board members were named directors at Marvell Tech. Brad Bush had been a director at Cavium since July 2016 and previously was the chief financial officer at SolarCity, now part of Tesla ( TSLA ), and at Cypress Semiconductor (CY). Edward Frank also became a Cavium director in July 2016 and had been the co-founder and chief executive of an internet startup, Cloud Parity, and also had been a vice president of Macintosh hardware systems engineering at Apple (AAPL) following a stint at Broadcom Corp (AVGO).
